bib.title: InterCode: Standardizing and Benchmarking Interactive Coding with Execution Feedback
bib.venue: 37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023) Track on Datasets and Benchmarks

question: Does giving an LLM coding agent execution feedback over multiple turns improve code generation, and how can interactive coding be evaluated in a standard, reproducible way?
hypothesis: Interactive code generation with execution feedback beats static one-shot generation.
contributions: We develop InterCode, a new, universal framework for interactive code generation, which provides ease of use, extensibility, and safety.
Using InterCode, we perform a comprehensive evaluation of state-of-the-art models and identify several avenues for improvements.
We release our framework as a new benchmark along with useful empirical tools to customize any new static code datasets into interactive tasks.

method.summary: InterCode wraps code execution in Docker as a gym-style POMDP (code = action, execution output = observation, reward in [0,1]). Environments for Bash (NL2Bash), SQL (Spider) and Python (MBPP) are built; seven LLMs are prompted Single Turn, Try Again (retry with execution output and reward until reward 1 or n turns), ReAct, and Plan & Solve. No training.
method.task: interactive code generation with execution feedback (Bash, SQL, Python)

datasets.name: InterCode-SQL (Spider 1.0 dev)
datasets.source: Spider, CC BY-SA 4.0; converted to MySQL with sqlite3mysql
datasets.preprocessing: kept only question and gold SQL; lower_case_table_names enabled; test user with all privileges

datasets.name: InterCode-Bash (NL2Bash)
datasets.size: 200 commands in 4 disjoint sets (3 grounded to custom file systems, 1 file-system agnostic)
datasets.preprocessing: subset of 1000 commands with >=4 utilities; filtered non-UNIX/Linux and unsupported (ssh, sudo, time, GUI); under-specified commands given concrete names/paths; deprecated flags updated

datasets.name: InterCode-Python (MBPP)
datasets.preprocessing: none; unit tests inherited. Not evaluated in the experiments

inference.decoding: API sampling; OpenAI n=1 completion, PaLM candidate_count=1
inference.samples: one run per item as far as stated; Table 7 reports standard errors over file systems 2-3-4 for Bash, number of runs not stated
inference.prompting: Single Turn zero-shot; Try Again zero-shot with task description; ReAct and Plan & Solve with few-shot demonstrations (ReAct example shown; Plan & Solve 'three examples'); templates Tables 11-14

parameters.default Bash reward: 0.34*TF-IDF cosine similarity of outputs + 0.33*(1-erf(#fs mismatches)) + 0.33*share of commonly changed paths with equal md5sum
parameters.SQL reward: Jaccard IoU of record lists scaled by (Kendall tau+1)/2

other.human_baseline: authors (all proficient in SQL), 15 random SQL tasks, n=10, human decides when to submit

metrics.name: Success Rate (SR)
metrics.definition: proportion of task episodes where r = 1

metrics.name: Error %
metrics.definition: percentage of non-admissible actions (cannot be parsed/executed) across task episodes

metrics.name: Turns
metrics.definition: average number of turns per task episode

eval.protocol: Each model run on all tasks per strategy; Spider hardness buckets (Easy/Med/Hard/Extra) and 4 Bash file systems reported; no significance test; standard errors only in Table 7.

prompts.text: ## TASK DESCRIPTION You are a {self.language} code generator helping a user answer a question using {self.language}. The user will ask you a question, and your task is to interact with a {self.setting} system using {self.language} commands to come up with the answer. ... DO NOT WRITE ANYTHING EXCEPT FOR CODE in your response. ## OUTPUT DESCRIPTION Given your {self.language} command input, the system will then give back output formatted as follows: Output: <string> Reward: [0, 1] ... The closer the reward is to 1, the closer your {self.language} command is to the correct answer.

Interact with a {self.setting} system using {self.language} queries to answer a question. Use interleaving Thought, Action, Observation steps. Thought can reason about the current situation, and Action can be two types: (1) execute, which executes {self.language} code on the {self.setting} system (2) submit, which indicates that the previous observation is the answer
For the following user question, let's first understand the problem and devise a plan to solve the problem. Then, let's carry out the plan to solve the problem step by step.

limits: Try Again feeds the reward (computed against the gold output) back to the agent and stops the episode automatically when reward = 1; ReAct and Plan & Solve stop on the agent's own judgment. The headline gains are therefore retry against an oracle, not self-verification (Fig 2 caption: the purpose is to explore how capable agents are at error correction from feedback).
SQL Single Turn is zero-shot with no schema; the schema ablation (Table 5) shows much of the SQL gain is information gathering (single turn 10.5 -> 67.9 once schema is given).
Only Bash and SQL evaluated; Python environment built but not benchmarked. Environments limited to Bash, SQL, Python.
CTF: Sec 5.3 says 100 objectives; Limitations says the CTF dataset is limited to just four task instances.
Plan & Solve + Refine tested on only 44 tasks; human baseline only 15 tasks by the authors.
Models plateau in later turns and repeat actions; context handling is the failure point.
Single run per configuration at temperature 0; standard errors only for Bash file systems 2-4.
Models are 2023 vintage (text-davinci-003, gpt-3.5-turbo, gpt-4, Vicuna-13B).
